title: Representable locally finitely presented isomorphisms descend along space limits
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their fppf sheaves and small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. All indexing sets are small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale chart from a quasi-compact scheme; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback over every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, respectively the relative diagonal for a morphism, is quasi-compact. A morphism is affine if it is representable and its pullback over every affine scheme test has affine scheme source [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over $S$ with affine transition morphisms, and suppose the fppf sheaf $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ is an algebraic space with its specified projections. Fix $i_0\in I$. Let $Y_0\to X_{i_0}$ and $T_0\to X_{i_0}$ be representable morphisms of algebraic spaces, with $Y_0$ and $T_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $g_0:Y_0\to T_0$ be an $X_{i_0}$-morphism locally of finite presentation, meaning that it is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. If $g_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X$ is an isomorphism, there exists $i\ge i_0$ such that $g_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 084S (lemma-descend-equality), with all hypotheses of Situation 084R (situation-descent) explicit.

proof.text: Restrict to $J=\{i\in I:i\ge i_0\}$. It is nonempty and directed. Any compatible family over $J$ extends uniquely over $I$: at $j\in I$, choose $k\ge j,i_0$ and project the $k$-component; a common upper bound makes this independent of $k$. Thus the given limit is unchanged. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $a:U_0\to X_{i_0}$ with $U_0$ affine using [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement]. For $i\in J$ put $U_i=X_i\times_{X_{i_0}}U_0$. The maps $U_i\to X_i$ are surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Each $U_i$ is an affine scheme: it is the pullback of the affine map $X_i\to X_{i_0}$ to the affine scheme $U_0$. Likewise $U_i\to U_j$ is affine for $i\ge j\ge i_0$, being the pullback of $X_i\to X_j$ to $U_j$. Here the statements that the pullbacks are schemes and affine are exactly the representability and affine scheme-test conditions, as in [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 084S (lemma-descend-equality), proof, affine etale reduction; Situation 084R.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] the scheme limit $L=\varprojlim_{i\in J}U_i$ exists. It represents $U=X\times_{X_{i_0}}U_0$. Indeed, for each scheme $V$ over $S$, a point of $U(V)$ is a point $u_0\in U_0(V)$ together with a compatible family $x_i\in X_i(V)$ whose $i_0$-component is $a(u_0)$. This is precisely a compatible family of points of $U_i(V)$, and hence, by the scheme-limit universal property, a unique map $V\to L$. These correspondences commute with every map of test schemes and with the projections, so identify $h_L$ with $U$ as fppf sheaves. Use this identification to write $U=\varprojlim U_i$.

source.place: Tag 084S (lemma-descend-equality), proof, affine etale reduction; Situation 084R.

proof.text: Put $P_0=Y_0\times_{X_{i_0}}U_0$ and $Q_0=T_0\times_{X_{i_0}}U_0$. Both are schemes by representability of $Y_0,T_0$ over $X_{i_0}$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The affine scheme $U_0$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; thus $P_0,Q_0$ are qcqs by the fibre-product assertion of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], applied over $X_{i_0}$. The map $Q_0\to T_0$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] to $g_0$ with target chart $Q_0\to T_0$ and source chart $1_{P_0}:P_0\to Y_0\times_{T_0}Q_0=P_0$. It says exactly that $h_0:P_0\to Q_0$ is locally of finite presentation as a scheme morphism.

source.place: Tag 084S (lemma-descend-equality), proof, affine etale reduction; Situation 084R.

proof.text: Every $U_i$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-limit-isomorphism-descent] to the system $(U_i)_{i\in J}$, with initial base $U_0$ and the morphism $h_0:P_0\to Q_0$. Its limit base change is the pullback to $U=X\times_{X_{i_0}}U_0$ of the assumed isomorphism over $X$, so is an isomorphism. The theorem gives $i\ge i_0$ such that $h_i:P_0\times_{U_0}U_i\to Q_0\times_{U_0}U_i$ is an isomorphism. The fibre-product universal property identifies this map with the pullback of $g_i:Y_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i\to T_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i$ along $U_i\to X_i$.

source.place: Tag 084S (lemma-descend-equality), proof, affine etale reduction; Situation 084R.

proof.text: Write $Y_i=Y_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i$, $T_i=T_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i$. For a scheme $V$ and $t\in T_i(V)$, its image in $X_i(V)$ lifts to $U_i$ on an fppf cover $V^{\prime}\to V$ by [lem-a1-representable-etale-fppf-local-lifting]. Over this cover the inverse of $h_i$ gives a lift of $t$ to $Y_i$. On the double overlap the same $U_i$-lift from either projection may be used to compare any two lifts: the base change of $g_i$ to $U_i$ is invertible, so those lifts agree. Therefore the sheaf condition for $Y_i$ glues the lift uniquely over $V$. Similarly any two lifts over $V$ agree after the cover and hence agree. The resulting bijections $Y_i(V)\to T_i(V)$ commute with restriction, since the lifts are unique. They give an inverse natural transformation to $g_i$, hence an isomorphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. This is the required finite stage.
